small_guidance:
- The conv_transpose3d call is now the dominant cost (fast_p≈0.47 with the GN fusion already in place). Tuning BLOCK/num_warps of the existing fused kernel will not close the gap; only marginal gains are possible (e.g. autotune over BLOCK ∈ {2048, 4096, 8192} and num_warps ∈ {4, 8} with num_stages=2-3).
- Consider folding the weight/bias loads outside the inner-tile loop by loading per-channel scalars once per program (one program per (n,g) already), broadcasting across spatial tiles to cut redundant loads.
- Switch the two-pass to a single-pass Welford to halve global memory traffic on the input tile.
large_guidance:
- Replace nn.ConvTranspose3d with a custom Triton scatter-add kernel: one program per (N, IC tile, input-spatial tile) computing the outer product `input[n,ic,d,h,w] * weight[ic,oc,kd,kh,kw]` and atomically scattering into the output grid at the strided/padded positions. This is where the headroom is — the torch conv_transpose3d is the bottleneck.
- Alternatively, formulate ConvTranspose3d as a gemm: reshape weight to (IC, OC*kd*kh*kw), matmul with input (N*D*H*W, IC), then col2im-scatter into the output. Fuse the bias add + Swish into the col2im epilogue.
- Fuse GroupNorm + HardSwish as a second kernel (already done) but try persistent-per-(N,G) with the conv-transpose output buffered in shared memory if the group footprint fits; otherwise keep as-is and focus all effort on the conv-transpose replacement.
